senses.d: Designed to be worn or placed inward.
ex: the wrong side of a garment or of a piece of cloth

senses.d: In a way that isn't right; incorrectly, wrongly.
ex: I spelled several names wrong in my address book.

senses.d: Something that is immoral or not good.
An instance of wronging someone (sometimes with possessive to indicate the wrongdoer).
ex: Can she excuse my wrongs with Virtue's cloak? Shall I call her good when she proves unkind?

senses.d: The incorrect or unjust position or opinion.
ex: I blame not her: she could say little less; She had the wrong.

senses.d: The opposite of right; the concept of badness.
ex: Thus much of this will make Black white, foul fair, wrong right, Base noble, old young, coward valiant.

senses.d: To treat unjustly; to injure or harm; to do wrong by.
ex: The dealer wronged us by selling us this lemon of a car.
Thou dost then wrong me, as that slaughterer doth Which giveth many wounds when one will kill.

senses.d: To deprive of some right, or to withhold some act of justice.
To slander; to impute evil to unjustly.
